subject.title: feat(memory-core): optional cross-encoder rerank stage for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw accept this `MemoryRerankProvider` SDK API, `memoryRerankProviders` manifest gate, exclusive slot, and builtin-only scope as the public contract for memory reranking?
rationale: The implementation is plausible and well-proven, but public plugin APIs and manifest contracts become compatibility commitments after release and the RFC intentionally leaves the contract shape for maintainers.

options.title: Approve After Rebase
options.body: Accept this SDK seam direction, require a conflict-resolved rebase on current main, and rerun the focused memory/plugin/docs validation before merge.

options.title: Revise The Contract
options.body: Ask for a different capability declaration, keyed provider model, qmd scope, or SDK shape before this becomes public API.

options.title: Pause Behind RFC
options.body: Keep this PR open but unmerged until the RFC settles, or close it only if maintainers reject the direction outright.

recommendation.title: Approve After Rebase
recommendation.body: Accept this SDK seam direction, require a conflict-resolved rebase on current main, and rerun the focused memory/plugin/docs validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a plugin SDK and memory-host public-contract decision, and recent path history points to steipete on those boundaries.
